purpose: This is a grid where you place two points and watch a right triangle build itself between them. You see why the distance is the square root of dx squared plus dy squared, then use the same idea in a 3D box and in stories like a ladder.

stops.title: Points A and B
stops.text: In Plane mode, drag the rings A and B. They snap to whole numbers. When they are not in the same row or column, a green horizontal leg and a red vertical leg meet at a right angle, and the blue side is the distance d.
stops.try: Drag B to different places. When does the triangle disappear?

stops.title: Three modes
stops.text: Plane works with two points. 3D box measures the longest rod in a box. Stories uses a picture from real life. The Next button in the steps switches modes for you: step 3 is the box, step 4 is stories.
stops.try: Press 3D box, then press Plane again to come back.

stops.title: Squares on the sides
stops.text: Draws a square on each side of the triangle. The two small squares (green and red) add up to the big blue one: dx squared plus dy squared equals d squared. It only shows when A and B are in different rows and columns.
stops.try: Switch it on and move B. Check that the two small areas always add to the big one.

stops.title: Distance challenges
stops.text: Pick a target distance, such as AB = 5, and place B to hit it. The readout shows how many different leg pairs work, and says whether the squares add up to too little or too much if you miss.
stops.try: Choose AB = 5 and find two different places for B that work.

stops.title: Try a box
stops.text: In 3D box mode, use the Length, Width and Height sliders, or pick a preset or a challenge. The readout works the box out in two right triangles: first the base diagonal f, then the long diagonal d.
stops.try: Pick Preset 3 x 4 x 12. The longest rod is exactly 13.

stops.title: Pick a story
stops.text: Stories are a ladder on a wall, the longest rod in a box, blocks across town and the diagonal of a screen. Each has stages. At each stage the yellow side is the unknown.
stops.try: Choose A ladder on a wall and read the question first.

stops.title: Add or subtract
stops.text: If the unknown side is the hypotenuse, add the squares of the legs. If it is a leg, subtract. Choose one. A wrong choice shows why it fails, and a right one moves to the next stage. Start over resets the story.
stops.try: Choose the wrong operation on purpose to read the explanation.

stops.title: Quick check
stops.text: A few questions at the end. A wrong answer explains why and you can try again.

teacher: Project step 2 with squares on and ask what the three areas show. Then challenge AB = 5 and ask how many ways it can be done. Common slip in stories: adding squares when the unknown is a leg. Ask 'is the yellow side the longest side?' first.
